IBM
A technology company building advanced quantum processors using superconducting qubits.<SEP>A technology company actively building advanced quantum processors.

Quantum Processors
Advanced hardware systems being built by companies like IBM and Google.<SEP>Advanced hardware units built using superconducting qubits to achieve quantum supremacy.

Quantum Computing
A rapidly emerging technology and field that harnesses the laws of quantum mechanics to solve complex problems.<SEP>A rapidly emerging technology that harnesses the laws of quantum mechanics to solve problems too complex for classical computers.

Google
A technology company building advanced quantum processors using superconducting qubits.<SEP>A technology company actively building advanced quantum processors.

Richard Feynman
A physicist who originally inspired the field of quantum computing in 1982.<SEP>The physicist who originally inspired the field of quantum computing in 1982.

Superconducting Qubits
A technology utilized in the construction of advanced quantum processors.<SEP>The technological components used in the construction of advanced quantum processors.

Quantum Mechanics
A branch of physics whose laws are harnessed by quantum computing.<SEP>The scientific laws and principles harnessed by quantum computing to perform complex computations.

Classical Computers
Traditional computing devices that are unable to solve certain complex problems handled by quantum computing.<SEP>Traditional computing systems that are unable to solve the highly complex problems addressed by quantum computing.

1982
The year in which Richard Feynman originally inspired the field of quantum computing.<SEP>The year in which the field of quantum computing was originally inspired by Richard Feynman.

Quantum Supremacy
The milestone of quantum computing capability that companies aim to achieve using advanced quantum processors.<SEP>The milestone of solving problems beyond the capability of classical computers, targeted by companies building advanced quantum processors.
